classification: Assistant-authored educational base-case judgments, not company guidance, analyst consensus, investment recommendations or price targets.

methodology.scope: These defaults apply only to a fresh or explicitly reset current-company draft matching the named snapshot. Existing user edits and historical/frozen experiments must not change.
methodology.growth: Except for the documented AAOI staged profile, year 1 uses growth, then annual growth fades linearly to terminalGrowth in year 10. It is not a constant ten-year CAGR. Economic checks show the resulting size and CAGR.
methodology.margin: Except for the documented AAOI staged profile, reported baseline EBIT margin fades linearly to targetMargin by year 10, except an explicitly disclosed starting-EBIT normalization. Target margin is operating EBIT after ongoing R&D, SBC and depreciation, not gross margin, EBITDA or an adjusted EPS margin.
methodology.reinvestment: Net reinvestment = max(0, change in revenue / salesCapital). Ratios are independent forward judgments, not mechanically copied from total sales/book-capital or capex/sales. Gross maintenance capex, R&D capitalization and replacement cycles are not separately modeled.
methodology.tax: Normalized blended operating cash-tax estimates apply to positive EBIT only. Reported accounting effective rates are evidence, not marginal cash-tax forecasts; tax-loss carryforwards are not modeled.
methodology.wacc: WACC is an assumed nominal required return, never issuer-reported. Use observed USD Treasury 5.09% on 2026-10-16, an explicitly chosen 4.5% equity premium informed by January 2026’s 4.23% estimate, and assumed beta, target market-value debt weight and debt spread. The January premium is not an October observation. Round model WACC to 0.5 percentage points; betas and weights are not measured live. TSM uses a separately disclosed assumed currency conversion.
methodology.terminal: Stable growth is modest nominal growth in the model currency, below WACC and terminal ROIC. Terminal reinvestment/NOPAT = g/ROIC. Mature returns normally fall from explicit-period productivity; a discrete year-11 transition remains a simplification.
methodology.bridge: otherClaims=0 and otherAssets=0 are unreviewed numerical placeholders, not verified absence or fair values. No reviewed flags, financing reconciliation or share conversion is implied. Explicit specialist and claim-related gates take precedence over these defaults.
methodology.validation: Deterministic operating-path checks and lower/higher operating cases are model sanity tests, not calibrated probabilities. No stock price or future return is used to choose assumptions.
methodology.evidence: Primary issuer releases and exact current filing sources available by 2026-10-17 anchor judgments. Historical annual data are latest-reported context and may include recasts; structural breaks are disclosed.
methodology.companySpecificPath: AAOI fresh research uses the documented staged capacity profile. Growth/margin progression and capital-intensity terminal fade are applied to every deterministic and simulated case. Other companies retain the original linear transition.

rationale.growth: 8% starts above FY2025 growth of 6.4% but below the latest 16% quarter. Services and replacement demand support growth; the installed base and hardware maturity argue for an immediate fade rather than extrapolating one strong quarter.

rationale.terminalGrowth: 2.5% nominal USD is a mature-state assumption with limited real expansion, well below the high-growth starting rate and the discount rate; it is not a company forecast.
rationale.years: 10 years is the common model horizon so company economics can be compared; rates and margins fade over this period. The number is a modeling convention, not a source fact.

AAOI.classification: conditional staged capacity research assumptions; not a validated fair-value estimate
AAOI.summary: Provisional research assumptions only. A high-risk capacity-led turnaround in datacenter optics, with substantial funding needs before durable GAAP profitability.

rationale.growth: 60% is year 1 growth. The staged profile then uses 40%, 30%, 20%, 15%, 10%, 8%, 5%, 3%, and 2.5% at these defaults. Quarter 3 guidance and capacity expansion support a front-loaded structure; the annual path is analyst judgment, not management guidance. Each simulated initial-growth input changes the whole same weighted path.
rationale.targetMargin: 12% mature GAAP EBIT margin is reached in year 6. At the reported starting loss, the staged path is −5%,0%,5%,8%,10%,12% before maturity. This is a conditional utilization and operating-leverage judgment; no non-GAAP net margin is substituted.
rationale.tax: 25% applies only to positive modeled EBIT. This is a normalized mature rate; no tax refund or verified NOL benefit is assumed during losses.
rationale.salesCapital: 0.8x is initial incremental sales/capital, requiring $1.25 investment per $1 extra revenue in years 1–2. It rises to 1.6x by years 6–7 as capacity is used. Years 8–10 fade capital intensity toward (1 + terminal growth) × margin × (1 − tax) / terminal ROIC, ending at 1.084x at defaults to align year 10 and terminal economics. The whole path is an explicit assumption, not a reported ratio.
rationale.terminalROIC: 10% assumes capital utilization improves in maturity but grants no excess return versus the high constant model discount rate.

HOOD.summary: Brokerage equity cash flows retain customer and regulatory capital.
HOOD.classification: Dated filing evidence with explicit analyst assumptions

rationale.growth: Analyst scenario, not management guidance: fade elevated growth toward3% terminal growth.
rationale.growthZh: 分析假设而非管理层指引：较高增长率逐步降至3%的永续增长率。
rationale.targetMargin: Pretax earnings attributable to common owners; recurring SBC stays an expense.
rationale.targetMarginZh: 普通股股东应占税前收益率；持续性股权薪酬保留为费用。
rationale.salesCapital: HOOD uses0.55 revenue per dollar of incremental required common equity, near dated revenue/book-common-equity0.49–0.52; buffers exceed legal minimum capital.
rationale.salesCapitalZh: HOOD每增加一美元所需普通股资本支持0.55美元收入，接近当期收入/普通股账面权益0.49–0.52；资本缓冲高于法定最低要求。
rationale.wacc: This control is cost of equity, not WACC; no enterprise-value bridge.
rationale.waccZh: 该参数表示股权成本，并非加权平均资本成本；不使用企业价值桥接。
rationale.terminalROIC: Terminal return on required common equity governs sustainable earnings retention.
rationale.terminalROICZh: 永续期所需普通股资本回报率决定可持续的利润留存。
rationale.terminalGrowth: HOOD: terminalGrowth = 0.03 is an explicit analyst starting assumption, not a reported future outcome. See the company sources and sensitivities.
rationale.tax: HOOD: tax = 0.21 is an explicit analyst starting assumption, not a reported future outcome. See the company sources and sensitivities.
rationale.otherClaims: Disclosed minority, preferred and other claims are included once. Existing employee options, when present, use the separate dated allocation model.
rationale.otherAssets: Nonoperating investments use the selected filing amount or an explicitly documented omission. Assets whose earnings are already included are not added again.
rationale.years: HOOD: years = 10 is an explicit analyst starting assumption, not a reported future outcome. See the company sources and sensitivities.

bridgeLimitations: Net interest is core revenue. The model deducts all operating expenses, retains stock compensation, and excludes other income, including the 2026 RVI deconsolidation gain and investment gains. The June base also removes minority earnings. Customer assets are excluded and issued restricted shares are not counted twice.

Preexisting corporate cash is retained as operating capital. Trust funding costs are already in net interest and its debt is not deducted again. The June corporate convertible and assumed retained proceeds are treated separately.

Customer cash, customer securities and regulatory collateral are not shareholder surplus assets. Existing corporate cash is retained as operating capital; the model does not assume that the legal minimum is a sufficient operating buffer.

Employee options and warrants use a conservative full-share dilution proxy. The model adds 3.033979 million options and 8.74 million warrants once, without deducting a separate option value. Ignored exercise proceeds can reduce value by at most approximately $0.28 per modeled share; out-of-the-money awards make this proxy more conservative.

Stock compensation remains an expense in projected earnings. Unissued RSUs are additional shares; already-issued restricted stock is not added again. Future grants and repurchases may change the share count.

Revenue per dollar of new required common equity is a modeling assumption, not a regulatory formula. Required operating capital may grow differently from revenue as margin lending, credit cards and trading activity change.

The June statement rounds common shares to 899 million. The annual employee-option count is carried forward because June lacks a complete option rollforward. Share-count rounding is approximately 0.12% or less; the carried option count is a labeled conservative proxy.

The June corporate financing bridge adds $1,757 million of assumed retained proceeds: $2,200 million issued, less $30 million issuance costs, $123 million capped-call premium and $290 million concurrent buyback. Cash is fungible; this is an allocation assumption, not an identified bank balance.

The corporate convertible is deducted once at its disclosed $2,208 million fair value. No conversion shares are added on top. The operating Credit Card Funding Trust is treated separately: its financing cost is already in net interest, so its debt is not deducted a second time.

No separate asset value is credited for the capped calls. Their $123 million historical premium, about $0.13 per modeled share, is a sensitivity reference, not a bound on current value. Scenarios materially above the $174.42 conversion strike need an updated option and capped-call treatment.

bridgeLimitations: The model uses the issuer-reconciled fee revenue, including its share of equity-method fee businesses. Common pretax earnings equal fee-related earnings attributable to BAM plus investment and other income net of interest. Subtracting cash taxes gives distributable earnings less the stock-compensation addback. All post-reorganization common shares are included; BN ownership and minority interests are not deducted again.

Owner earnings already include financing costs and proportionate ownership. The model does not add all investments or cash, or subtract consolidated-fund debt and minority interests a second time. Investments whose earnings are included receive no separate asset-value addback.

The denominator includes all outstanding BAM common shares after the reorganization, excluding treasury shares. Brookfield Corporation’s ownership of BAM is not another minority-interest deduction. Options on Brookfield Corporation are a different issuer’s shares and are not added to BAM.

The June-quarter 14.9 million incremental diluted-EPS shares serve as a proxy for combined option and escrow dilution, not a reported period-end award count. Zero to twice this proxy tests an effect of roughly 1% on value per share. No separate option-value deduction is applied. Already-issued restricted stock and escrow-share cancellations must not be double counted.

Owner earnings retain stock-compensation costs and already reflect attributable ownership and financing costs. Consolidated fund assets, fund borrowings and minority interests are not added or deducted a second time.

The forecast assumes that each dollar of new required common equity supports $3 of fee revenue. The terminal 25% return applies to new incremental equity, not the entire existing book-equity balance. This lower terminal capital efficiency raises required retention; it does not assume an unfunded jump in the existing capital stock.

Fee revenue and owner earnings are reconciled non-GAAP business measures. The 2022 predecessor year is contextual because the reorganization and bundled compensation addback limit comparability; the 2023–2025 owner-earnings series is directly reconciled.

rationale.growth: 18% initial revenue growth is an analyst scenario supported by 17% FY2026 growth and 30% latest-quarter growth, then fades. $664bn remaining performance obligations are multi-year contracts, not current revenue or guaranteed profit.

rationale.terminalGrowth: 3% long-run nominal growth, below the discount rate, with growth fading as the infrastructure footprint matures.
rationale.terminalROIC: 15% mature marginal return is an analyst normalization, not the recent book return. It requires eventual utilization and lower incremental capital intensity; continuing today’s build intensity indefinitely would reduce value substantially.
rationale.years: Ten-year explicit forecast. Annual and TTM are dated conditional starting points; future financing, construction schedules and customer credit performance are scenario risks.

FY2026 revenue increase of $9,958m divided by cash capex of $55,663m less depreciation of $7,623m is 0.207; TTM capex is $75,660m. rationale.wacc: 10% analyst required return reflects AI contract concentration, execution risk and substantial debt financing; it is not a quoted market WACC.
rationale.terminalGrowth: 3% long-run nominal growth, below the discount rate, with growth fading as the infrastructure footprint matures.
rationale.terminalROIC: 15% mature marginal return is an analyst normalization, not the recent book return. It requires eventual utilization and lower incremental capital intensity; continuing today’s build intensity indefinitely would reduce value substantially.
rationale.years: Ten-year explicit forecast. Annual and TTM are dated conditional starting points; future financing, construction schedules and customer credit performance are scenario risks.
rationale.otherClaims: Disclosed minority, preferred and other claims are included once. Existing employee options, when present, use the separate dated allocation model.
rationale.otherAssets: Nonoperating investments use the selected filing amount or an explicitly documented omission. Assets whose earnings are already included are not added again.

rationale.growth: 30% initial growth fading toward 3% is an analyst scenario below nine-month 2026 growth 145%; it recognizes AI power demand without extrapolating one year of rapid deployment indefinitely.

Installation losses, service obligations and competition limit profitability.
rationale.tax: 23% normalized tax is an analyst assumption for sustainable profitability. Historical low taxes reflect losses and allowances; no separate NOL asset is added.
rationale.salesCapital: 1.5 x incremental sales to capital funds gross manufacturing, inventory and receivable growth without assuming recurring customer-advance financing. Nine-month 2026 capex 231 m and working-capital expansion argue against software-like capital efficiency. Existing deposits are separately reserved once.
rationale.wacc: 11.5% discount rate is an editable analyst required return reflecting concentrated project demand, manufacturing execution, fuel economics, leverage and dilution; it is not live market-derived WACC.
rationale.terminalGrowth: 3% terminal growth assumes a mature power-equipment business and requires ongoing reinvestment.
rationale.terminalROIC: 15% marginal terminal capital return assumes an established manufacturing and service franchise with continuing competition; historical loss years are not calibration targets.
rationale.years: Ten forecast years allow deployment growth and margins to mature while capital intensity remains explicit.
rationale.normalizationDelta: Starting operating income excludes own-share product profit on sales to unconsolidated affiliates that the filing eliminates below EBIT; raw GAAP figures remain visible. TTM uses the rounded 16.9 m current-period elimination.
rationale.otherClaims: Disclosed minority, preferred and other claims are included once. Existing employee options, when present, use the separate dated allocation model.
rationale.otherAssets: Nonoperating investments use the selected filing amount or an explicitly documented omission. Assets whose earnings are already included are not added again.
